fields.name: buttonOrNone
fields.comment: Move producer stores -1. Click producer leaves it untouched; no consumer on the native path reads it.

fields.name: x

fields.name: y
fields.comment: Client-area Y, cvtdq2ps of the integer pixel coord from the LL hook.

fields.name: timestamp

fields.name: ctorInitOne
fields.comment: Constructor seeds every slot with 1; no producer or consumer touches it. Purpose unknown.

fields.name: message
fields.comment: Raw Windows message number as delivered to the LL hook. The click sender packs its low 7 bits into the wire header byte.

fields.name: sourceFlags
fields.comment: MSLLHOOKSTRUCT.flags verbatim. Click sender uses bit 0 only; move sender writes the whole low byte per sample.

fields.name: interfaceId
fields.comment: Parent interface id. NOTE on the withheld OInterfaceComponent.COMPONENT_TYPE: there is NO component-type field on this class. On Linux, jag::game::InterfaceComponent::CreateByType@0xc39300 dispatches a 29-entry jump table (types 0x00..0x1c) in which five slots (1,2,7,8,25) share one invalid target and create nothing, while the other 24 each construct a distinct C++ subclass - 13 inline with their own vtable and 11 through a dedicated pooled factory with its own pool global and element stride. The type is consumed to pick the subclass and never written back, so the class identity IS the type and is recoverable only from the vptr. The value previously shipped as a type (Linux +0xe) is the PARENT LAYER COMPONENT ID (jag::opcode::_if_getlayer, jag::InterfaceManager::GetParentLayer). That whole enumeration is recorded on the Linux CreateByType function and CANNOT be carried here: vtable and pool addresses are per-binary, so a PE vptr->type table must be re-derived from the PE's own factory before anything is emitted. Do not re-add a COMPONENT_TYPE offset.

fields.name: itemId
fields.comment: ITEM_ID = 0x180. Getter @0xb93f0 MOV EAX,[RCX+0x180]; setter @0xb9410 CMP EDX,[RCX+0x180] / MOV [RCX+0x180],EDX then MOV byte[RCX+0x191],1. SUBCLASS OVERLAP: the region above 0x180 is laid out independently by different InterfaceComponent subclasses, so these offsets do not all coexist in one object. The item-bearing subclass uses {itemId 0x180 dword, stackSize 0x188 qword, dirty byte 0x191}; the model-bearing subclass uses {modelId 0x190 dword, modelObject 0x198 qword}. modelId (0x190..0x193) and the 0x191 dirty byte physically overlap, which is why the dirty byte is documented here rather than declared as a field.

fields.name: stackSize
fields.comment: STACK_SIZE = 0x188. Getter @0xb9400 MOV RAX,[RCX+0x188]; setter @0xb9430 MOV [RCX+0x188],RDX then MOV byte[RCX+0x191],1. 64-bit field; the engine reads it as an int. SUBCLASS OVERLAP: the region above 0x180 is laid out independently by different InterfaceComponent subclasses, so these offsets do not all coexist in one object. The item-bearing subclass uses {itemId 0x180 dword, stackSize 0x188 qword, dirty byte 0x191}; the model-bearing subclass uses {modelId 0x190 dword, modelObject 0x198 qword}. modelId (0x190..0x193) and the 0x191 dirty byte physically overlap, which is why the dirty byte is documented here rather than declared as a field.

fields.name: modelId
fields.comment: MODEL_ID = 0x190. Getter @0xb9ab0 is MOV EAX,[RCX+0x190]; setter @0xb9a90 is MOV [RCX+0x190],EDX - a full dword. SUBCLASS OVERLAP: the region above 0x180 is laid out independently by different InterfaceComponent subclasses, so these offsets do not all coexist in one object. The item-bearing subclass uses {itemId 0x180 dword, stackSize 0x188 qword, dirty byte 0x191}; the model-bearing subclass uses {modelId 0x190 dword, modelObject 0x198 qword}. modelId (0x190..0x193) and the 0x191 dirty byte physically overlap, which is why the dirty byte is documented here rather than declared as a field.

fields.name: lastClickSampleTime

fields.name: camera
fields.comment: OClient.CAMERA = 0x19858. A large family of CS2 camera opcode handlers at 0x95820-0x96790 all load *(client+0x19858); the object carries a Client back-pointer at +8 as on Linux. NOTE the Windows Client is 0x53818 bytes (Linux 0x53358) and the manager-slot band at 0x19830..0x19A00 is NOT in Linux order, so no offset may be carried across platforms.

NOTE the Windows Client is 0x53818 bytes (Linux 0x53358) and the manager-slot band at 0x19830..0x19A00 is NOT in Linux order, so no offset may be carried across platforms.

fields.name: interfaceList
fields.comment: OClient.INTERFACE_LIST = 0x198c0. MiniMenu::DoOpComponentInner@0xe0f30 loads it three times and passes it as this to InterfaceManager::IfButtonXInner. NOTE the Windows Client is 0x53818 bytes (Linux 0x53358) and the manager-slot band at 0x19830..0x19A00 is NOT in Linux order, so no offset may be carried across platforms.

fields.name: itemStackList
fields.comment: OClient.ITEMSTACK_LIST = 0x198f8. FUN_000b7230 ground-item tile lookup; also referenced by REBUILD_NORMAL. NOTE the Windows Client is 0x53818 bytes (Linux 0x53358) and the manager-slot band at 0x19830..0x19A00 is NOT in Linux order, so no offset may be carried across platforms.

fields.name: spotAnimManager
fields.comment: OClient.SPOTANIM_MANAGER = 0x19948. The per-tick pass FUN_0018e490 updates it in the Linux slot order players/npcs/projectiles/itemstacks/SPOTANIM/.../hints. NOTE the Windows Client is 0x53818 bytes (Linux 0x53358) and the manager-slot band at 0x19830..0x19A00 is NOT in Linux order, so no offset may be carried across platforms.

fields.name: button
fields.comment: Button identifier. 0 is the LEFT button, not "no button" -- see the entry-point comment on SendEventMouseClick. SendEventMouseClick puts only (button != 0) on the wire, in bit 15.

fields.comment: Wire coordinate pair. This is the pair SendEventMouseClick clamps and sends, and the pair the camera/interface consumer reads.

fields.name: uiX
fields.comment: Second coordinate pair, read by the minimenu / interaction consumers instead of x/y. Never sent on the wire.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.comment: Monotonic clock snapshot; both senders delta-encode against the previous sent sample.

fields.name: ctorInitOne
fields.comment: Constructor seeds every slot with 1; no observed producer or consumer touches it. Same unexplained field as NativeMouseSample.ctorInitOne.

fields.name: valueMapBase

fields.name: hashTableBuckets

The value map sits at owner+0x98 and the buckets at mapBase+0x8, but the engine measures HASH_TABLE from the ClientVarDomain base, which is owner+0x88, giving 0x10+0x8 = 0x18. The 0x98 was measured from the setter's arg-2 owner instead, so this only became resolvable once OMainLogicManager.CLIENT_VAR_DOMAIN was established. Matches Linux 0x18.

fields.comment: PLANE_VEC_END = 0x168. @0x3c49cc MOV RAX,[R10+0x168]

fields.comment: LINK_HEIGHT_PLANE_COUNT = 0x1d0. SampleTileLinkHeightOffset@0x3c48ef CMP R11,[RCX+0x1d0]

fields.comment: LINK_HEIGHT_GRID = 0x1d8. @0x3c4935 MOV RAX,[RBX+0x1d8]. Indexing: plane*0x4000 + col*0x100 + row*4, cell is two i16

fields.comment: PLANE0_BRIDGE_GRID = 0x1e8. @0x3c4a35 MOV RAX,[R10+0x1e8] on the plane==0 bridge branch

fields.name: moveListener
fields.comment: eastl::function bound to this; registered into the InputHandler native-mouse-move listener vector. Invoker pushes the move ring.

fields.name: clickListener
fields.comment: eastl::function bound to this; registered into the InputHandler native-mouse-button listener vector. Invoker pushes the click ring.

fields.name: clickRing
fields.comment: Source ring drained by SendNativeMouseClick, exactly one entry per send.

fields.name: clickRingWrite
fields.comment: Producer cursor. Post-increment wraps at the slot count; on collision with clickRingRead the producer advances the read cursor, dropping the oldest sample.

fields.name: clickRingRead
fields.comment: Consumer cursor. Empty test is clickRingRead == clickRingWrite; SendNativeMouseClick advances it itself after emitting.

fields.name: moveRing
fields.comment: 200 NativeMouseSample slots, same 0x30 layout as clickRing. Drained in a loop into one variable-length movement-history packet per flush.

fields.name: vtable
fields.comment: VTABLE = 0x0. The manager is dispatched virtually as (**(code**)(*mgr + 8))(mgr,...) from the per-cycle update @0x00027520, so offset 0 holds the vtable pointer

fields.name: client
fields.comment: CLIENT_REF = 0x8. Add reads *(mgr+8) and indexes it with Client-sized displacements (+0x19990, +0x18d28, +0x19978, +0x18d40); its caller obtained the manager from the Client

fields.name: firstNode
fields.comment: FIRST_NODE = 0x10. Intrusive list head. On insert, Add writes node[0] = mgr+0x10 (the sentinel) and threads the new node through the tail pointer at mgr+0x18

fields.name: lastNode
fields.comment: Tail pointer of the intrusive list whose head sentinel is mgr+0x10

fields.name: poolFreeListHead
fields.comment: SpotAnimManager node pool, base at manager+0x20. The allocate-or-recycle helper (ELF 0x129780, called from Add via LEA RDI,[RBX+0x20]) reads exactly four words: [pool+0x00] free-list head (popped first, *node becomes the new head), [pool+0x08] bump-allocation cursor, [pool+0x10] bump-allocation limit (cursor == limit -> fall back to the heap), [pool+0x18] element stride (added to the cursor). Manager-relative that is +0x20/+0x28/+0x30/+0x38, and the PE carries the identical quadruple at the identical offsets. WITHHELD: the engine's OSpotAnimManager.POOL_START / POOL_END have NO correct mapping onto this structure - it is a free-list plus a bump allocator, not a start/end pair. The shipped ELF values (POOL_START 0x30, POOL_END 0x48) are provably wrong: 0x30 is the bump LIMIT, and 0x48 is past the end of the pool object entirely (the pool occupies 0x20..0x3f; 0x50 is LIST_SIZE). Both keys stay withheld on both platforms until the engine defines which two words it wants. Do not re-add 0x30/0x48.

fields.name: poolBumpCursor
fields.comment: Bump-allocation cursor of the node pool based at manager+0x20; see poolFreeListHead.

fields.name: poolBumpLimit
fields.comment: Bump-allocation limit of the node pool. The engine's OSpotAnimManager.POOL_START was shipped as this offset on the ELF, which is a misnaming - see poolFreeListHead.

fields.name: poolElementStride
fields.comment: Element stride added to the bump cursor; last word of the pool quadruple. The pool object ends at 0x40, so the shipped POOL_END 0x48 lies past it.

fields.name: listSize
fields.comment: LIST_SIZE = 0x50. Add increments *(mgr+0x50) by exactly one per node linked in. Independently lands on the offset the ELF table also carries

fields.name: varId
fields.comment: OPlayerVarDomain.VAR_ID / OClientVarDomain.VAR_ID = 0x0. FindOrCreateEntry@0xfdadc MOV dword[RAX],ECX. Shared node shape for both var domains

fields.name: varValue
fields.comment: OPlayerVarDomain.VAR_VALUE / OClientVarDomain.VAR_VALUE = 0x8. FindOrCreateEntry@0xfdb18 LEA RAX,[RDI+0x8]

fields.name: childArrayBegin

fields.name: childArrayEnd

fields.name: rmouseUpBegin
fields.comment: RMOUSE_UP = 0x210. Slot 5. 0x78bae0 clears the right-button state then walks +0x210/+0x218 (WM_RBUTTONUP @0x78a70f)

fields.name: mouseWheelBegin
fields.comment: MOUSE_WHEEL = 0x2e0. Slot 7. FUN_007895f0 (5-arg) reads +0x2e0/+0x2e8; called from OnScrollWheel @0x78bce0

fields.name: keyDownBegin
fields.comment: KEY_DOWN = 0x348. Slot 8. FUN_00789710, called from OnKeyDownInner @0x33dd0

fields.name: keyUpBegin
fields.comment: KEY_UP = 0x3b0. Slot 9. FUN_007897c0, called from OnKeyUpInner @0x34130

fields.comment: CLIENT = 0xc0. Client ctor @0x1d15f MOV [RDI+0x18e40],RDI, i.e. Input+0xc0; read back as the Client in OnKeyDownInner

fields.name: graphNode
fields.comment: DISPROVED 949-4 - do not re-add. The engine's OLocationContainer.STATIC_LOCATIONS_RBTREE_SENTINEL (0x8) and STATIC_LOCATIONS_RBTREE_BEGIN (0x10) are withheld: LocationContainer has no red-black tree. +0x8 is the Entity base's GraphNode pointer and +0x10 is the Entity kind discriminator byte (confirmed on the ELF ctor @0x494f40, which writes a pointer at +0x8 and a BYTE 9 at +0x10). Both shipped values also collided exactly with this object's ENTRY_LOCATION_PTR_OFFSET (0x8) and ENTRY_STRIDE (0x10) constants, which is where the numbers came from. Locations live in the three category vectors (multi 0xb0, primary 0xc8, tertiary 0xe0) plus the dispatch-slot table at 0xf8.

fields.name: vtable
fields.comment: DISPROVED 949-4 - do not re-add. The engine's OCombinedLocationSection.RENDER_NODE (0x270), RENDER_NODE_CTRL (0x268) and PARENT_COMBINED_LOCATION (0x330) are withheld: all three were copied verbatim from jag::game::Location and land past the end of this object. sizeof is 0x110 on the ELF (deleting dtor @0x4b9560: MOV ESI,0x110 before JMP operator delete) and the complete-object destructor enumerates every refcounted member without a render-node shared_ptr among them. The section reaches its renderable indirectly through its GraphNode. Recovering it means modelling that hop, not naming an offset.

fields.name: isHidden
fields.comment: OLocation.IS_HIDDEN = 0x18f. CORRECTS the shipped 0x18e, which was an unverified 949-1 carry on BOTH platforms. Nothing in the ELF reads Location+0x18e at all (a scan for CMP byte[reg+0x18e],0 returns zero matches), while +0x18f is read 20 times; on the PE the only +0x18e read is in FUN_00723f30, an unrelated class, against five +0x18f reads that all sit in Location methods. Semantics: +0x18f is the early-out 'skip this location' gate at the top of the render and pick paths. ELF pick test FUN_00481e70 opens with CMP byte[RDI+0x18f],0 / JNZ -> return 0; the PE analogue FUN_003bfb00 opens with CMP byte[RCX+0x18f],0 / JNZ -> bail, followed by the verified MOV RDI,[RCX+0x330] (parentCombinedLocation) and CMP qword[RDI+0x968],0 (CombinedLocation.renderModel) - instruction-for-instruction the same shape as the ELF site. IS_DELETED is the separate byte at 0x18d.

fields.name: meshComponents
fields.comment: ORenderModel.MESH_COMPONENTS = 0x268 (NEWLY DERIVED on the PE 949-4; the Windows table had no value). Entity pick-test vtable thunk @0x39e770: MOV RDI,[RCX+0xc68] (the verified Entity.renderModel), then @0x39e7c0 MOV RCX,[RDI+0x268], @0x39e7c7 LEA RDX,[RDI+0x30] (the verified WORLD_TRANSFORM), @0x39e7db MOV R8,[RCX], @0x39e7e1 ADD R8,0x8, CALL 0x4e4630 = MeshTrianglePickTest - the same function whose arguments established the MeshComponent and MeshData offsets. The engine's own consumer performs exactly this chain (read slot, deref once, +8, then {begin,end}), so this slot is what MESH_COMPONENTS denotes. Control-flow identical to the ELF site FUN_00481e70@0x481f70.
